issue.description: A trailing fragment shorter than FAN_EVENT_METADATA_LEN was marked consumed without setting lost=true. The caller therefore could not distinguish the discarded bytes from a completely parsed chunk and might not request reconciliation.
issue.fix: Mark coverage lost before consuming the short trailing suffix, so the caller widens recovery to a full observation.
issue.assumption: The kernel normally returns complete fanotify records; this is a fail-closed defense for malformed/truncated chunks.

regression_test.name: scan_first_hint_parser_marks_short_trailing_fragment_as_lost
regression_test.fixture: One valid synthetic parent-handle event followed separately by each 1-to-23-byte invalid suffix length.
assertions: all input bytes are accounted as consumed
the short suffix sets lost=true and requests widening to reconciliation

focused_new_test.command: nice -n 19 ionice -c 3 env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo test --offline scan_first_hint_parser_marks_short_trailing_fragment_as_lost -- --nocapture

related_parser_tests.command: nice -n 19 ionice -c 3 env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo test --offline scan_first_hint_parser -- --nocapture

coverage_limits: The regression test validates the parser's loss signal; it does not inject a truncated record from the kernel, which promises whole records from read().
The grouped parser test run contains the new regression and three related parser tests; it is not the full Rust suite or runtime fault matrix.
